submission.justification: Radiator-R3 at 3 cm thickness provides the best pion/kaon separation performance among all viable candidates. With a separation power of σ = 3.963, it significantly outperforms Radiator-R2's best result (σ = 2.801 at 2 cm). Although Radiator-R1 showed the highest initial separation at baseline (σ = 4.6), it was eliminated due to failing the mandatory aging constraint. R3 at 3 cm represents the optimal balance, achieving the highest separation among the two radiators that meet the durability requirements. This thickness maximizes the Cherenkov photon yield while maintaining optical quality, as evidenced by the performance decrease at both thinner and thicker configurations.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R3 is one of the three candidate radiators evaluated in the study.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%
requirements.evidence: R3_passes_aging_constraint = 1, confirming that Radiator-R3 meets the durability requirement. Radiator-R1 was eliminated as R1_passes_aging_constraint = 0.
Recommended thickness of 3 cm is within the specified range of 1-6 cm.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R3 at 3 cm achieves σ = 3.963, which is the best separation among all viable candidates (best_separation_sigma = 3.963, best_radiator_number = 3, best_thickness_cm = 3). This significantly exceeds R2's best performance of σ = 2.801.
